title: Service Credential Evidence Orchestration for Offline Audits
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines how Redwood collects, normalizes, and packages service credential evidence (service accounts, keys, certificates, ephemeral tokens, and KMS operations) for offline, auditors-facing evidence review. The goal is to ensure reproducible, tamper-evident bundles that satisfy regulatory auditors (ISO 27001, SOC2, and regional data residency requirements) while minimizing operational impact on running services.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-managed service identities and long/short-lived credentials across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Includes evidence types: secret material change logs, rotation events, KMS envelope ops, identity provider assertions, issuance and revocation records for ephemeral tokens, and privileged authorization requests.
- Excludes end-user PII content inside request payloads; evidence packaging strips or references payload-level data per data-residency rules.

Principles:
- Integrity first: every evidence bundle must include cryptographic integrity metadata (hashes, signing key id).
- Minimal exposure: do not include raw secrets in artifacts. Use signed attestations and KMS-derived proofs instead.
- Traceable provenance: every record must map back to a service, actor, and causal event ID.

Evidence sources (inventory):
- secrets-store-rotation-service logs (/var/log/secret-rotation.service.log)
- KMS audit stream (kms.audit.events) with envelope IDs and ECDSA signatures
- Service-account-manager (SAM) change events: create/update/deactivate
- Authz-subsystem: role binding changes and policy decision logs (PDP requests/responses)
- Ephemeral-token-issuer: issuance, TTL, revocation feeds
- Audit-collector: consolidated event index (index level: tenant, region, timestamp, event_hash)

Required fields for each record (normalization schema):
- record_id: stable UUID
- service_id: service::<name>
- actor_id: user|service::<id>
- event_type: rotation|issue|revoke|policy_change|kms_encrypt|kms_decrypt
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339
- provenance_chain: comma-delimited list of upstream record_ids
- evidence_hash: sha256hex of canonicalized payload
- signature_ref: key-id@kms or signing-cert-id
- locality_tag: region or residency-zone

Evidence retention & residency rules (high level):
1) Short-lived ephemeral issuance records: retain 90 days globally unless linked to an ongoing investigation.
2) Rotation and revocation records: retain 3 years for enterprise contracts; default 12 months for self-serve orgs.
3) KMS envelope metadata and signatures: retain 7 years (cryptographic proof) with residency mirroring of the key material.
4) Audit indices and canonical payload references: follow per-tenant data-residency policy; where prohibited, store only hashes and index pointers in Redwood-hosted systems and place full artifacts in customer-controlled storage.

Offline Audit Bundle Format (manifest-driven):
- Each bundle is a tar.gz containing:
  - manifest.json (plain text JSON describing contents and metadata)
  - records/ (ndjson files, one file per evidence type; canonicalized)
  - proofs/ (signatures, kms-attestations, signed-timestamps)
  - metadata/ (collection-runbook.txt, collector-version.txt, region-tag.txt)
- manifest.json required keys: bundle_id, collected_at, collector_version, included_record_types, records_counts, top_level_hash, signer_key_id, residency_declaration

Sample manifest.json (snippet):
{
  "bundle_id": "bundle-20260501-6a7d9e",
  "collected_at": "2026-05-01T14:32:11Z",
  "collector_version": "audit-collector/3.2.1",
  "included_record_types": ["rotation", "kms", "ephemeral_issue"],
  "records_counts": {"rotation": "142", "kms": "2,134"},
  "top_level_hash": "sha256:8b4f...",
  "signer_key_id": "kms-orange:projects/redwood/keys/evidence-sign-01",
  "residency_declaration": "customer-eu-only"
}

Collection orchestration (high-level steps):
1) Kickoff: Audit lead creates an AuditRequest in the evidence-requests queue with scope, tenant, residency constraints, and required ETA.
2) Pre-check: automated validator verifies requested scope against retention policy and residency (reject or escalate if disallowed).
3) Dry-run: collector performs a dry extraction to estimate bundle size and checks for PII exposure; report back to lead.
4) Collect: collector performs canonical normalization and writes ndjson records to ephemeral staging in encrypted disk.
5) Prove: collector requests KMS to produce an attestation (envelope metadata + signature).
6) Sanitize: runs PII/redaction ruleset; any removed content gets replaced by a referenced hash and a justification.
7) Sign & Seal: generate top-level manifest hash; sign with evidence-signing key in KMS; append signer cert + timestamp oracle entry.
8) Secure transfer: push to auditor destination via SFTP/AS2 or customer-controlled object store; generate receipt and archival ticket.
9) Audit closure: persist references in evidence-index and set retention timers; notify stakeholders.

Automation playbooks (examples & CLI):
- Dry-run: audit-collector dry-run --scope tenant=mycorp --since 2026-01-01 --residency eu
- Collect: audit-collector collect --request-id RQ-12345 --out /tmp/bundles/RQ-12345
- Sign: audit-sign --bundle /tmp/bundles/RQ-12345 --kms-key projects/redwood/keys/evidence-sign-01
- Transfer: audit-transfer push --bundle /tmp/bundles/RQ-12345.tar.gz --dest s3://audits-redwood/receipts/ --encrypt true

Example NDJSON record (canonicalized rotation event):
{"record_id":"4c2a7e10-77c9-4b1a-a2b8-e8d3f9d3958f","service_id":"service::token-issuer","actor_id":"service::rotation-agent","event_type":"rotation","timestamp_utc":"2026-04-29T03:12:22Z","provenance_chain":"a9f1...","evidence_hash":"sha256:6b7a...","signature_ref":"kms-orange:envelope-12345","locality_tag":"eu-central-1"}

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Security Evidence Council (SEC): final approver for restricted residency declarations and exceptions.
- Audit Collector Owner (eng-infra): maintain collector code, runbook, and test fixtures.
- Oncall Security (security): escalate PII exposure or integrity failures.
- Customer Success: coordinates delivery and confirms receipt with external auditors.

SLOs and operational thresholds:
- Dry-run feedback latency: < 2 hours for requests under 100k records.
- Collection success rate: >= 99% (batches not failing canonicalization).
- Bundle transfer retry: up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff; alert after 3 failures.
- Evidence-sign latency: < 30s per bundle under normal KMS load.

Risk exceptions and approval flow (abbreviated):
1) Exception request raised in exception-tracker with justification and compensating controls.
2) SEC performs technical review within 3 business days.
3) If approved, create an exception artifact with TTL and automated enforcement (policy gate).
4) Expired exceptions are auto-rejected and collector enforces standard flow.

Forensic checks & integrity validation (auditor checklist):
- Verify manifest top_level_hash matches recomputed hash.
- Validate KMS signature chain and signer_key_id.
- Cross-check record counts and sampling of records against original index queries.
- Confirm residency_declaration and check that any full-artifact locations match customer-controlled storage where mandated.

Appendix A — Common troubleshooting steps:
- If collector fails canonicalization: run audit-collector inspect --request-id <id> to locate malformed records.
- If KMS attestation times out: fallback to pre-signed envelope metadata with SEC approval; file incident ticket.
- If transfer fails for residency reasons: engage customer success to request temporary transfer window or archive in customer VPC.

Appendix B — Sample query snippets for auditors (elastic-like DSL):
- rotation events in timeframe:
  {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"event_type": "rotation"}}, {"range": {"timestamp_utc": {"gte": "2026-01-01","lte": "2026-04-30"}}}]}}
